description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — October 9, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: openai/codex is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: openai/codex leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: openai/codex — 10 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 40.5 below its current daily pace, with 3 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 71 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
Kilo-Org/kilocode — No same-day commit after 366 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Check the receiver before relying on agent status lights
dailyInsight.insight: Pi 1.1.0 and Crush 0.98.0 report working, human-blocked and finished runs through the same OSC 7501 format. A supporting terminal can surface a request for attention without extracting it from each agent display.
dailyInsight.mechanism: Crush prioritizes permission, question and authentication dialogs over busy state. Pi reports the outcome after its session settles and distinguishes cancellation from completion. The terminal chooses how to display the structured reports.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: People working across several agent tabs gain a common signal for which one needs a response. Actual usefulness depends on receiver support and the path through any terminal multiplexer.

actions.audience: Builders using Pi or Crush across multiple terminal tabs
actions.label: Check the complete sender and receiver path
actions.instruction: Before relying on status indicators, check that the installed terminal supports OSC 7501 and that any intermediary forwards it. In a disposable task, observe a question, cancellation and completion, then check that the indicator clears. Keep normal conversation review until that path is demonstrated.
actions.effort: One short local compatibility check when a supporting receiver is available

receipts.title: Crush maps human waits and turn outcomes to program status
receipts.supports: Permission, question and authentication requests take precedence over working state; focus clears the recorded outcome.

receipts.title: Pi adds negotiated OSC 7501 reports
receipts.supports: Reports lifecycle and dialog state, distinguishes cancellation and negotiates receiver support.

receipts.title: Crush 0.98.0
receipts.supports: Published release contains the inspected status sender.

receipts.title: Pi 1.1.0
receipts.supports: Release published October 8 in Paris contains the inspected sender.

confidence.basis: Inspected pinned implementations and containing tags; five isolated upstream Pi formatter and support-reply tests passed.

dailyInsight.limitation: No complete sender-to-receiver session was run. Rex is an invitation-only beta; Ghostty parser support is not application display. Pi documents a tmux/screen forwarding limitation. Reported working and done states do not prove progress or correct output.
dailyInsight.falsifier: A pinned released sender failing to emit its documented blocked state, or a supported receiver showing stale waiting after cancellation or exit, would narrow the practical interoperability finding.
dailyInsight.watchNext: A released receiver and reproducible mixed-agent trace through waiting, cancellation, completion, focus and process exit, including any multiplexer.
